{{Short description|None}}
{{Main|Cross-country skiing at the Winter Olympics}}

[[Cross-country skiing (sport)|Cross-country skiing]] is a [[Olympic sports|sport]] that has been contested at the [[Winter Olympic Games]] since the inaugural games in [[1924 Winter Olympics|1924]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.olympic.org/uk/sports/programme/disciplines_uk.asp?DiscCode=CC |title=Cross Country Skiing |publisher=International Olympic Committee |access-date=2009-03-29}}</ref>

== Men ==
The numbers in brackets denotes cross-country skiers who won gold medal in corresponding disciplines more than one time. Bold numbers denotes record number of victories in certain disciplines.

== Discontinued ==

=== Women's 5 km ===
The 5&nbsp;km event ran from 1964 to 1998 before being replaced by the 10&nbsp;km event, which was reintroduced after the 10&nbsp;km had been discontinued following the 1988 Winter Olympics.

[[File:Marit Bjørgen.jpg|right|120px|thumb|[[Marit Bjørgen]] is the most successful Winter Olympian of all time. She is one of three Winter Olympians (and only woman) to win eight gold medals. In total, she won 15 Olympic medals – more than any athlete (male or female) in the history of Winter Olympics.]]

=== Medal sweep events ===
These are the [[podium sweep]]s; events in which athletes from one NOC won all three medals.
